articles.title: Legora is building the agentic operating system for legal work
articles.preview: Legora is developing an operating system designed for legal professionals. It leverages AI models to streamline legal workflows and improve efficiency.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO is risky business
articles.preview: Anthropic’s upcoming IPO reveals significant risks associated with developing advanced AI, particularly concerning potential harm and future market demand. The prospectus highlights numerous challenges the company faces as it navigates the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape.

summary.t: Anthropic’s IPO prospectus details over 90 pages of risk factors, exceeding typical corporate disclosures. The document identifies potential existential risks to humanity, including harm from its AI models. The company acknowledges the difficulty of guaranteeing adequate AI safety due to the technology’s complexity.

Several external factors pose risks to Anthropic’s operations. Opposition to data center development is growing, with 16 states considering moratoriums. The company’s reliance on extensive computing facilities also faces challenges, including potential shortages of electrical power and rising energy costs.
Anthropic faces potential legal challenges, mirroring concerns raised against competitors like OpenAI and Meta.

articles.title: Wall Street schließt im Plus : US-Anleger setzen wieder auf KI
articles.preview: Die Wall Street erlebte am Dienstag einen Aufwärtstrend, getrieben von der Hoffnung auf einen KI-Boom. Halbleiterwerte profitierten besonders von der positiven Stimmung.

summary.t: Die Wall Street schloss am Dienstag im Plus. Der Dow-Jones Index notierte bei 52.378 Punkten, der S&P 500 bei 7723 Zählern und der Nasdaq bei 26.478 Punkten.
Der bevorstehende Börsengang von Anthropic sorgte für Auftrieb bei Halbleiterwerten. Der Branchenindex stieg den dritten Tag in Folge. Chuck Carlson wies auf eine notwendige Gegenbewegung hin.

articles.title: Chart: Anthropic's cash pile towers over nearly every U.S. company
articles.preview: Anthropic, an AI lab, holds an unprecedented amount of cash, surpassing nearly all U.S. companies. The company’s massive cash reserves are expected to grow significantly with an upcoming IPO.

summary.t: As of June 30th, Anthropic reported $112.4 billion in cash and $19.3 billion in short-term investments, totaling $131.7 billion. This figure exceeds the cash reserves of every non-bank U.S. company except Berkshire Hathaway and Alphabet.

If Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) raises over $100 billion, the company’s total cash holdings could reach more than $230 billion. Existing investors will also participate in the IPO, meaning the company will not receive the full amount raised.

articles.title: AI debt fears ease ahead of Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon updates. Here's what to watch.
articles.preview: AI debt concerns have lessened recently, but new tests are expected. Several major tech companies, including Oracle, Alphabet, and Amazon, are reporting their financial results this week, which will be closely watched by investors.

summary.t: Following a period of volatility, concerns about artificial intelligence debt have eased somewhat. Investor confidence has improved, reflected in tightening credit spreads. Meta Platforms’ announcement of a $95 billion stock offering contributed to this positive shift, reducing its credit-default swap spreads.

Oracle will hold its Investor Day on Wednesday. Alphabet and Amazon.com are scheduled to report quarterly results on Wednesday and Thursday. Analysts anticipate Alphabet to report free cash flow of -$2.3 billion and Amazon to report -$9.9 billion in free cash flow.

Both Amazon and Alphabet are expected to continue reporting negative free cash flow in the second quarter. Analysts predict this trend will persist. Alphabet is projected to spend $55.2 billion on capital expenditures in the third quarter, while Amazon is expected to spend $58.7 billion.

summary.h: Focus on Hyperscaler Capex and Debt
summary.t: Analysts are closely monitoring the hyperscalers’ capital expenditure plans and free cash flow forecasts.

articles.title: Walmart says AI training is boosting confidence with the technology among its 2.1 million associates
articles.preview: Walmart’s massive workforce is showing increased confidence in AI technology following targeted training programs. The retailer’s survey of 2.1 million associates revealed a significant shift in attitudes towards AI’s potential in the workplace.

summary.t: A survey of over 1.7 million Walmart associates revealed that 77% of office-based staff are excited about AI’s potential to improve their work. Furthermore, 84% of U.S. frontline associates expressed confidence in using digital tools, largely due to AI-powered tools they now utilize.

Walmart partnered with Google and OpenAI to provide free AI certification programs for its associates. Those completing OpenAI training reported a 27% confidence gain in using AI. The company has also given associates certificates and training programs.
Walmart’s approach focuses on using AI to reduce friction and enhance human capabilities, rather than replacing jobs.

articles.title: Retell uses OpenAI models to help power 100M monthly calls
articles.preview: Retell is utilizing OpenAI models to handle 100 million monthly calls. The company has achieved a significant revenue run rate of $1.6 million per employee thanks to its use of Codex.

articles.title: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership
articles.preview: Nvidia and AMD are committing a combined $4 billion to Meta, bolstering the company's ambitious AI infrastructure plans. This significant investment signals a deepening strategic partnership between the tech giants.

summary.t: Meta announced an initial $35 billion in public equity offerings, with plans to raise an additional $60 billion through a market program. This brings the total investment sought by Meta to $95 billion.
Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering. The investment will support Meta’s expansion of Vera Rubin and Vera CPU deployment.

articles.title: OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
articles.preview: OpenAI and Oracle are deepening their collaboration. This expansion will integrate OpenAI’s applications into ChatGPT and fuel new Oracle products.

articles.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
articles.preview: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to a large group of employees to manage costs related to its significant investment in artificial intelligence. This move is part of a broader effort to streamline operations and focus on key growth areas.

summary.t: Microsoft is offering a voluntary exit program to approximately 60,000 employees across the U.S., Canada, India, and the United Kingdom. The offer is available to workers with an experience level of 70 or below, representing roughly 27% of the company’s total workforce of 223,000.

The company’s investment in AI infrastructure, particularly supplying cloud services to companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, has led to substantial capital expenditures. Capital spending for the September quarter is projected to exceed $50 billion, a significant increase from the $34.9 billion spent in the prior year.
Microsoft is simultaneously implementing a voluntary retirement program and laying off 4,800 employees, reflecting a strategic shift towards a more flexible workforce.

articles.title: From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect'
articles.preview: Anthropic, the creator of Claude, is planning a massive initial public offering (IPO) that could be the largest in history. This event is expected to have a significant ripple effect throughout the tech industry, particularly impacting valuations and investment strategies.

summary.t: Anthropic is seeking to launch an IPO with a potential valuation exceeding $1 trillion, placing it alongside companies like Saudi Aramco and SpaceX. The company’s rapid revenue growth, reaching $11.56 billion in the second quarter, is driving this ambitious valuation. Concerns exist that a poor debut could trigger a market correction, potentially impacting valuations across the AI sector.

Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter, a significant improvement after previous losses. The company holds nearly $132 billion in cash and has secured substantial investments from major players like Amazon, Broadcom, and Google. These investments include $77 billion in notes and a $15 billion investment from Nvidia.

Approximately half of Anthropic’s revenue comes from partnerships with cloud providers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet. The company faces competition from OpenAI and a broader range of model providers, including open-weight models. Despite this competition, Claude Opus 5.5 Max currently outperforms other models on key benchmarks.

Experts express concern about potential market saturation due to rising hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure. Some analysts believe the AI boom is fueled by readily available credit, and a drying up of liquidity could negatively impact the S&P 500. Despite these concerns, Snowflake is exploring alternative, lower-cost models, highlighting the ongoing innovation and competition within the AI landscape.

articles.title: Halbleiterwerte im Aufwind: Naher Anthropic-Börsengang treibt Wall Street an
articles.preview: Die Wall Street erlebte einen positiven Wochenstart, getrieben von der erwarteten Börsengang-Pläne von Anthropic. Zudem veröffentlichten mehrere KI-Riesen ihre Bilanzzahlen, was zu Kursgewinnen führte.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones schloss bei 52.362 Punkten, ein Anstieg von 0,3 Prozent. Der S&P 500 stieg um 0,7 Prozent auf 7677 Punkte und der Nasdaq gewann 0,8 Prozent auf 26.169 Punkte. Damit endeten zwei Wochen der Verlustserie.

Anthropic, ein KI-Unternehmen, hatte die Unterlagen für seinen Börsengang in den USA eingereicht. Die Pläne erzeugten Optimismus im Technologiesektor, nachdem die KI-Bullen zuvor durch hohe Kosten und Zinsen geschwächt waren.
Der Philadelphia SE Semiconductor stieg um 2,8 Prozent.

articles.title: Sparen für den KI-Boom: Microsoft bietet jedem vierten Mitarbeiter eine Abfindung an
articles.preview: Microsoft bietet derzeit Abfindungen an, um die Belegschaft flexibler zu gestalten. Dies geschieht im Zuge massiver Investitionen in Künstliche Intelligenz.

summary.t: Microsoft hat insgesamt 60.000 Mitarbeitern Abfindungen angeboten, was etwa einem Viertel der weltweiten Belegschaft entspricht. Die Berechtigung gilt für Mitarbeiter in den USA, Kanada, Indien und Großbritannien. Personalchefin Amy Coleman erklärte, dass dies das zweite Abfindungsprogramm innerhalb eines Jahres ist.

articles.title: Prediction market traders say an Anthropic IPO is near-certain this year after company filed with SEC
articles.preview: Anthropic, the AI company, has filed to go public, significantly increasing the likelihood of an IPO this year. Prediction markets show a strong consensus that the company will likely complete its IPO before the end of 2026.

articles.title: As AI becomes more fractured, one names stands out: AMD
articles.preview: The artificial intelligence sector is experiencing instability, with several companies facing significant declines. AMD is currently standing out as a strong performer amidst this turmoil.

summary.t: Several AI-focused companies, including CoreWeave (-15.5%) and IREN (-20%), have experienced sharp drops this year. This instability is fueled by concerns surrounding data center spending and is impacting chipmakers, particularly AMD.

AMD shares fell 8.1% due to Meta's financing plans and a supply warning from Lam Research. Despite sector-wide anxieties, AMD remains a standout based on specific criteria, including revenue growth and profitability.
Consensus estimates predict AMD’s Q3 earnings at $1.94 billion and revenue at $13.06 billion, representing significant year-over-year growth of nearly 62% and 41%, respectively.

AMD CEO Lisa Su announced plans to substantially increase supply in 2027 to meet the growing demand from AI orders. This highlights the current imbalance between supply and demand within the AI chip market.
AMD’s stock is experiencing high volatility, with earnings moves ranging from 38% to 9% over similar windows.

articles.title: KI-Unternehmen Anthropic beantragt Börsengang und warnt vor Risiken
articles.preview: Das KI-Unternehmen Anthropic plant einen Börsengang im November. Dieser Börsengang könnte einer der größten aller Zeiten werden und wird von Investmentbanken unterstützt.

summary.t: Anthropic plant den Börsengang. Das Unternehmen hat die notwendigen Unterlagen bei der SEC eingereicht. Der Börsengang könnte in der Woche ab dem 16. November stattfinden und das Unternehmen mit bis zu 2 Billionen Dollar bewerten. Aktien werden am Nasdaq unter dem Tickersymbol "ANT" gehandelt.

Der Umsatz von Anthropic stieg im ersten Halbjahr 2026 von 1,2 Milliarden auf 16,3 Milliarden Dollar. Gleichzeitig vergrößerte sich der Nettoverlust drastisch auf 80,7 Milliarden Dollar, hauptsächlich aufgrund hoher Kosten für Rechenzentren.
Anthropic listet vier Hauptrisiken im Zusammenhang mit KI auf: Missbrauch, Verlust der Kontrolle, autoritärer Missbrauch und wirtschaftliche Verwerfungen.

articles.title: Rasantes Wachstum, rote Zahlen: Anthropic legt Informationen für möglichen Weltrekord-Börsengang offen
articles.preview: Anthropic, ein führendes KI-Startup, plant einen Börsengang. Dieser könnte das bisherige Börsengeschäft des Raumfahrtkonzerns SpaceX übertreffen.

summary.t: Anthropic verzeichnete im ersten Halbjahr 2026 einen enormen Anstieg des Umsatzes von 1,2 Milliarden US-Dollar auf 16,3 Milliarden US-Dollar. Dieser deutliche Zuwachs spiegelt das wachsende Interesse an den fortschrittlichen KI-Modellen des Unternehmens wider.

Trotz des hohen Umsatzanstiegs wies Anthropic einen dramatischen Nettoverlust von rund 80,7 Milliarden US-Dollar aus. Dieser massive Fehlbetrag ist deutlich höher als der Vorjahr-Minus von 13 Milliarden US-Dollar.
Anthropic plant den Börsengang an der Nasdaq unter dem Tickersymbol "ANT".

articles.title: Fanatics teams up with OpenAI for new AI-powered shopping suggestion feature
articles.preview: Fanatics is using AI to help shoppers navigate more than 1.5 million items of sports merchandise, with a Shop the Look feature powered by OpenAI Codex.

articles.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
articles.preview: OpenAI is releasing data related to complex scientific problems. The goal is to collaborate with researchers for further understanding and verification.

articles.title: Meta announces $95 billion stock offering to fund AI expansion
articles.preview: Meta announced a massive $95 billion stock offering to fuel its rapid expansion into artificial intelligence. This move comes as other tech giants also seek significant capital to invest in AI infrastructure.

summary.t: Meta plans to initially raise $35 billion through an underwritten public equity offering. Subsequently, the company intends to raise an additional $60 billion utilizing an at-the-market program.
Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, and Broadcom expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion in Meta shares.
Estimates suggest AI-related capital spending could total approximately $7.6 trillion globally between 2026 and 2031, encompassing compute, data centers, and power.

articles.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
articles.preview: CodeRabbit is utilizing GPT-6.1 Sol to bolster security. The tool is focused on identifying and addressing vulnerabilities within large codebases.

articles.title: SK Hynix shares jump 11% after record quarterly profit, outperforming broader market
articles.preview: SK Hynix achieved a record-breaking quarterly profit, significantly exceeding expectations. The company announced substantial shareholder returns, driving a dramatic surge in its stock price.

summary.t: SK Hynix reported a staggering 327.9% increase in revenue and a 632.1% rise in operating profit compared to the previous year. The company announced plans to return approximately 100 trillion won to shareholders through a combination of dividends and buybacks. A 14 trillion won third-quarter dividend, including a special dividend of 30 trillion won, was approved. The company also announced a 20 trillion won share buyback program, with 10 trillion won to be cancelled.

SK Hynix paused its review of potential fundraising for Solidigm due to market volatility. The company intends to return gains from its Kioxia investment through a special dividend. The company anticipates continued structural supply-demand imbalance in the memory market through 2030. Mehdi Hosseini of Susquehanna International Group maintains a neutral rating, favoring Micron and Samsung.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Nvidia-Zulieferer vervielfacht Gewinn
Jim Cramer warns investors not to get fooled by the latest AI stock rally
articles.preview: Jim Cramer warns investors against celebrating the recent AI stock rally, citing ongoing financial challenges within the sector. He believes the market’s enthusiasm is premature and doesn’t fully account for significant risks.

summary.t: AI-related stocks experienced a second consecutive day of gains, driven by a $63 billion financing deal for Anthropic to purchase Broadcom’s computing hardware. This followed a rally sparked by Anthropic’s S-1 filing.

Jim Cramer remains worried about smaller AI infrastructure companies, known as neoclouds, which are taking on substantial debt to fund data center construction. Rising interest rates are intensifying concerns about their ability to manage these debts.
Cramer questioned the reassurance provided by the $63 billion financing deal, suggesting Anthropic is using borrowed funds to purchase Broadcom’s technology instead of paying with profits.
Cramer noted a calmer bond market, but predicted this could be temporary.

articles.title: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17
articles.preview: General Motors is set to migrate its stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq. This move is intended to align the company’s brand with its growing focus on technology and innovation.

summary.t: General Motors announced it will begin trading on the Nasdaq on November 17th. The company’s ticker symbol will remain ‘GM.’ Current shareholders do not need to take any action to complete the transfer.
This move reflects GM’s strategy of positioning itself as a technology-focused company. The company’s CFO stated Nasdaq is a ‘natural home’ for its listing as it grows.

articles.title: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
articles.preview: Amazon has issued a memo discouraging engineers from excessive use of AI tools, a trend they’ve termed "tokenmaxxing." The company is shifting its focus to measuring AI’s impact on long-term outcomes rather than simply tracking AI usage metrics.

summary.t: In September, Amazon circulated a memo to employees outlining revised guidelines for AI usage within the company. The memo, now publicly available, reflects a shift in how software development engineers and managers are expected to interact with AI tools. The company acknowledges AI's growing importance but emphasizes a need for careful consideration.

Amazon previously shut down an internal leaderboard after discovering employees were engaging in ‘tokenmaxxing’ – excessively using AI tools to gain recognition. The company now views metrics like token usage and AI tool adoption as potentially flawed and costly.
Instead of focusing on the quantity of AI tokens used, Amazon is prioritizing measuring long-term outcomes, such as feature velocity and successful product launches.

articles.title: Größter IPO Indiens: Jio Platforms startet Frontalangriff auf US-Tech-Giganten
articles.preview: Mit dem größten Börsengang der indischen Geschichte startet Jio Platforms einen Angriff auf US-Tech-Giganten. Die Nachfrage überstieg das Angebot bei Weitem, was auf ein großes Interesse an der Firma hindeutet.

summary.t: Jio Platforms hat mit dem größten Börsengang der indischen Geschichte begonnen. Ursprünglich war die Emission für 2024 geplant, wurde aber zweimal verschoben, da der Iran-Krieg eine Rolle spielte. Die Nachfrage war so groß, dass die Aktie 22-fach überzeichnet war und eine Nachfrage von über 77 Milliarden US-Dollar betrug.

Der Börsengang wurde mit dem Ziel gegründet, 1,5 Milliarden Menschen in Indien einen schnellen Internetzugang zu ermöglichen. Die Firma konnte rasch ihre Konkurrenz mit Kampfpreisen von nur 2 Dollar im Monat unterbieten. Im Juni zählte Jio 533 Millionen Nutzer, was etwa einem Drittel der indischen Bevölkerung entspricht. Der Konzern erzielt rund 90 Prozent seines Umsatzes im Telekommunikationsgeschäft. Im Geschäftsjahr 2025/26 erwirtschaftete das Unternehmen einen Gewinn von 3,2 Milliarden Dollar bei einem Umsatz von 15,5 Milliarden Dollar.

Andreas Lipkow und Jacques Abramowicz sehen im Börsengang einen wichtigen Vertrauensbeweis für den indischen Kapitalmarkt. Abramowicz betont, dass Indien seine Fähigkeit zur Finanzierung digitaler Unternehmen auf globaler Ebene zunehmend unter Beweis stellt. Lipkow betont die Signalwirkung des Börsengangs und die Verbindung von Technologie, Kunden und Cloud-Anwendungen.

Jio investiert verstärkt in künstliche Intelligenz und baut eigene Rechenzentren auf. Das Unternehmen betreibt auch eine eigene Sparte für Satelliten in niedriger Erdumlaufbahn, was zu einem Konkurrenzkampf mit SpaceX und Musk führt. Analysten mahnen zur Differenzierung und betonen, dass der Börsengang noch keinen strukturellen Wandel markiert.

articles.title: 40 DAX-Aktien jetzt rund um die Uhr handelbar
articles.preview: Die Deutsche Börse erweitert den Handel mit DAX-Aktien auf rund um die Uhr. Damit können Anleger nun auch außerhalb der regulären Börsenzeiten Aktien wie Siemens und SAP kaufen und verkaufen.

summary.t: Ab sofort können Anleger rund um die Uhr mit den 40 DAX-Aktien handeln. Der reguläre Handel auf Xetra läuft werktags von neun Uhr morgens bis halb sechs abends. Seit Dezember vergangenen Jahres sind bereits erweiterte Handelszeiten von acht Uhr morgens bis zehn Uhr abends möglich.
Der Handel in der Nacht und am Wochenende erfolgt über die Handelsplattform 360X. Die Commerzbank ist an dieser Plattform beteiligt. Die Abwicklung erfolgt über Clearstream-Konten.

articles.title: Zweijährige Rally vorbei: Chinas KI-Blase ist längst geplatzt - mit harten Folgen für Kleinanleger
articles.preview: Die KI-Blase in China ist platzt, was zu massiven Kursverlusten führt. Besonders Kleinanleger erleiden hohe Verluste.

summary.t: Der chinesische Aktienmarkt, insbesondere der STAR50-Index, hat in den letzten Monaten einen dramatischen Einbruch erlebt. Der Index ist in weniger als vier Monaten um 40 Prozent gefallen und hat rund 480 Milliarden Dollar an Marktwert vernichtet. Dieser Absturz ist deutlich stärker als in den westlichen Märkten.

Mehrere Faktoren haben zum Absturz beigetragen, darunter Sorgen über die Nachfrage nach KI-Technologien, Beschränkungen für chinesische Exporte und überzogene Bewertungen. US-Exportverbote spielten ebenfalls eine Rolle.

Besonders hart getroffen werden Kleinanleger, die beispielsweise den Roboterhersteller Unitree oder den Chiphersteller CXMT gekauft haben. Die Aktien dieser Unternehmen sind seit ihrer Einführung stark eingebrochen.

articles.title: Infineon baut für über eine Milliarde Euro Werk in Österreich aus
articles.preview: Infineon baut eine neue Produktionsanlage in Österreich aus. Der Chip-Hersteller investiert über eine Milliarde Euro in den Standort Villach.

summary.t: Infineon plant den Bau einer neuen Fertigung für Leistungshalbleiter in Villach, Kärnten. Die Investition beläuft sich auf 1,1 Milliarden Euro. Diese Anlage soll die Produktion schnellerer und größerer Halbleiter ermöglichen.

Die neuen Halbleiter basieren auf Galliumnitrid (GaN). Diese Technologie bietet eine höhere Schaltgeschwindigkeit und somit eine bessere Energieeffizienz im Vergleich zu Siliziumchips. Experten schätzen, dass der Markt für GaN-Chips bis 2031 um das Sechs-Fache auf 3,5 Milliarden Euro wachsen wird.

articles.title: Im Verbraucherschutz nachbessern: Temu kündigt nach Millionenstrafe der EU Änderungen an
articles.preview: Temu, der chinesische Online-Händler, steht vor einer erheblichen Strafe der EU. Das Unternehmen hat nun Zugeständnisse an die Europäische Kommission gemacht, um die Strafe zu mildern.

summary.t: Die Europäische Kommission verhängte im Mai eine Strafe von 200 Millionen Euro gegen Temu. Die Begründung war, dass das Unternehmen Verbraucher nicht ausreichend vor illegalen Produkten schütze und die Risiken auf seiner Plattform unterschätze, was gegen den Digital Services Act verstößt.
Um die Strafe zu vermeiden, hat Temu Änderungsvorschläge vorgelegt. Diese beinhalten eine zukünftige Prüfung der Empfehlungsalgorithmen, um die Verbreitung illegaler Produkte zu verhindern.

articles.title: Investors are doing just as well this year by shunning AI. How to invest if the tech trade keeps fizzling
articles.preview: Investors are shifting away from AI-related stocks, and a market index excluding these companies is now performing similarly to the broader S&P 500. This rotation is driven by concerns about the tech sector's performance and a broader trend of investors seeking diversification.

summary.t: A Goldman Sachs index excluding AI enablers has risen 12.4% through October 22nd, matching the S&P 500’s 12% gain. This index’s performance has become neck-and-neck with the standard S&P 500 following a rally in tech stocks on Monday.

The S&P 500 tech sector is down approximately 7% this month, while other sectors have shown resilience. Investors are avoiding debt and equity issued by companies like CoreWeave and Oracle. Companies involved in AI infrastructure, such as GE Vernova, Bloom Energy, and Vistra, have also experienced significant declines.
Investors are moving into defensive sectors, including State Street Consumer Staples, Health, Utilities, and Energy. Energy’s gains are partially attributed to the situation in Iran.
